figures.description: 學校的舞台上方掛著「英文話劇比賽」的布條。台上兩個穿戲服的學生正在演出：一個戴著皇冠的女生和一個舉著紙劍的男生面對面演戲。舞台左邊布幕外的後台，一個學生拿著劇本在小聲提詞。台下，三位評審坐在長桌後面看表演，桌上放著評分表；評審後面坐著五個觀眾。

questions.stem: 提示：學校舉辦英文話劇比賽，每班都要用英文演出一齣短劇。請仔細看下面的圖片，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段描述圖中話劇比賽的情形；第二段寫出你自己參加班級表演或上台演出的一次經驗，並說明你比較喜歡在台上演出還是在幕後幫忙，以及原因。

1.explanation_zh: 這一題有三個要求：第一段描述圖中話劇比賽的情形（台上演出的兩個學生、後台提詞的學生、台下的評審與觀眾）；第二段寫自己參加班級表演或上台演出的一次經驗，再說明比較喜歡在台上演出還是在幕後幫忙與原因。偏好要和自己的經驗連在一起，理由才有說服力。
evidence: 描述圖中話劇比賽的情形
寫出你自己參加班級表演或上台演出的一次經驗
說明你比較喜歡在台上演出還是在幕後幫忙，以及原因
1.strategy_zh: 第一段照「台上、後台、台下」的順序寫；第二段先用過去式寫一次表演經驗，再用 I prefer … to … 或 I would rather … than … 說明選擇，最後補一個理由或例子。
hints: 第一段：On the stage, a girl wearing a crown is …; Backstage, …
第二段：Last year, my class performed … I worked as …
偏好：I prefer working behind the scenes to acting on the stage because …

moves.zh: 描述圖中話劇比賽的情形
寫出你自己參加班級表演或上台演出的一次經驗
說明你比較喜歡在台上演出還是在幕後幫忙，以及原因

content.focus_zh: 第一段寫出台上演出的兩個學生、後台提詞的學生、台下的評審與觀眾中至少三項；第二段要有一次班級表演或上台演出的具體經驗，並清楚說出比較喜歡台上演出還是幕後幫忙，給出理由。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。
漏掉題目的主要要求或主旨模糊，多數句子空泛、重複或偏離題目。
空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

organization.focus_zh: 第一段由台上寫到後台，再寫到台下；第二段先寫經驗、後寫偏好，理由可用 First、Second 列出，結尾回扣題目。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。
段落大致分明，但有的地方跳接或重複，轉承語偏少或用得生硬。
重點排列混亂，前後句常接不起來，讀者不容易跟上。
看不出段落與順序，句子彼此無關。

grammar.focus_zh: 描述圖片用現在進行式；寫經驗用過去式（forgot、whispered）；比較台上和幕後時，prefer A to B、would rather A than B 的句型要完整。

bands.descriptor_zh: 句子幾乎沒有文法、標點錯誤，能交替使用簡單句、複句與不同的句首。
偶有時態、單複數或標點錯誤，但讀得懂意思；句型變化有限。
錯誤多到常讓人誤解意思，句子結構常不完整。
幾乎沒有正確的句子，無法理解。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 話劇、戲服、劇本、台詞、評審、觀眾等說法（play、costume、script、lines、judge、audience）要用對；audience 指一群觀眾時是集合名詞，不寫成 audiences。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。
字彙範圍偏窄、常重複同幾個字，偶有用字不當或拼錯，但不妨礙理解。
用錯字或拼錯字很多，常讓人看不懂。
幾乎每個字都用錯或拼錯，無法理解。

rubric.deductions_zh: 字數明顯不足（少於 100 個單詞）或沒有分成兩段，各扣總分 1 分；兩種情形同時發生只扣 1 分。離題或空白以 0 分計。

branches.prompt_zh: 那次表演是在什麼時候？為了什麼活動？
表演在哪裡舉行？台下有多少人？
你和哪些同學一起準備？你負責什麼？

你比較喜歡在台上演出還是在幕後幫忙？為什麼？

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The picture shows an English drama contest in the school hall. On the stage, two students in costumes are performing a short play. A girl wearing a crown is facing a boy who is holding up a paper sword. Backstage on the left, another student is holding a script and whispering lines to the actors. Below the stage, three judges are sitting at a long table with score sheets in front of them. Behind the judges, five students are watching the show.
Last year, my class also took part in this contest, and we performed a funny play about a lazy king. I did not want to act on the stage, so I worked backstage as the prompter. During the show, the boy who played the king suddenly forgot his lines. I quickly whispered the next sentence to him, and he finished the scene without any trouble. After the show, he thanked me in front of the whole class. Since then, I have preferred helping behind the scenes to acting. First, I do not have to stand in front of a big audience, so I feel relaxed. Second, I can help the whole team in a quiet way. Although the actors get more attention, the people backstage are just as important. In short, working behind the scenes is the best way for me to be part of a show.

paragraphs.function_zh: 描述圖片：由台上的演員寫到後台的提詞，再寫到台下的評審與觀眾

paragraphs.topic_sentence: Last year, my class also took part in this contest, and we performed a funny play about a lazy king.

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 第一段寫出台上、後台與台下的人，第二段有一次具體的提詞經驗與兩個理由（內容 4）；After、Since then、First、Second 讓順序清楚，但轉承較基本（組織 4）；時態與 prefer…to… 使用正確，句型變化有限（文法句構 4）；script、costume 等字正確，但整體多是常用字（字彙拼字 3）。總分 15，屬穩健版。

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
Under a banner announcing the English drama contest, the school stage has been transformed into a small kingdom. In the center, a girl wearing a golden crown is facing a boy who is raising a paper sword, and the two of them seem to be in the middle of a dramatic scene. What the audience cannot see, however, is happening just beside the left curtain. There, a student holding a script is whispering lines, ready to rescue any actor whose mind suddenly goes blank. Below the stage, three judges are sitting at a long table with score sheets in front of them, while five students behind them are watching closely. The picture reminds me that a play is far more than what happens under the lights; it depends just as much on the people the audience never notices.
Last spring, my class entered the same contest with a comedy about a lazy king, and I volunteered to be the prompter mainly because I was terrified of the stage. At first, my job seemed easy: I simply had to follow the script and stay silent. Halfway through our performance, however, the boy playing the king froze in front of three hundred people. For a few painful seconds, the hall was completely quiet. Without thinking, I whispered his next line twice, as loudly as I dared, and he picked it up so smoothly that most of the audience assumed the pause was part of the joke. We did not win first place, but our class won the prize for teamwork, and our king insisted that half of the credit belonged to me. Since that day, I have preferred working behind the scenes for two reasons. First, it suits my personality, since I can contribute fully without facing a sea of eyes. Second, the backstage crew sees the whole play at once, so I have learned to notice problems before they grow. Admittedly, actors receive the applause, and sometimes I envy them. Nevertheless, a show succeeds only when someone is quietly holding it together. In short, I would rather be that unseen helper than the star.

paragraphs.function_zh: 描述圖片：把舞台比喻成小王國，由台上的演員寫到布幕旁的提詞者與台下的評審、觀眾，最後點出幕後的重要
paragraphs.topic_sentence: Under a banner announcing the English drama contest, the school stage has been transformed into a small kingdom.

paragraphs.function_zh: 個人經驗與理由：擔任提詞者救場的經驗，再提出兩個理由、承認演員的光彩並表明選擇
paragraphs.topic_sentence: Last spring, my class entered the same contest with a comedy about a lazy king, and I volunteered to be the prompter mainly because I was terrified of the stage.

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 圖片描述有比喻與台上、後台、台下的細節，並點出幕後的重要；經驗段有救場的關鍵時刻、兩個理由與讓步（內容 5）；At first、however、Admittedly、Nevertheless 使敘事與論點層次分明（組織 5）；what 子句、so…that、would rather…than 等句型正確多樣（文法句構 5）；transformed、terrified、applause 用得貼切，但整體以常用字為主（字彙拼字 4）。總分 19，屬頂標版。

top.comment_zh: 第一段由台上演員、幕旁提詞的學生寫到台下評審與觀眾，並點出幕後的重要；第二段擔任提詞者救場的經驗細節豐富（three hundred people、whispered his next line twice），偏好與兩個理由清楚，含讓步並以 would rather … than 收尾。句型多變、用字精準，無錯誤。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段依台上、後台、台下的順序寫出演員、提詞者、評審與觀眾；第二段有當提詞者幫演國王的同學接詞的經驗，prefer helping … to acting 句型完整，兩個理由清楚，結尾回扣題目。全文無錯，但句型與字彙偏基本，細節較少。

top.comment_zh: 第一段由橫幅、台上的皇冠女生與紙劍男生，寫到左側幕邊提詞的學生，再到台下三位評審與五位觀眾，順序清楚，並點出「台下看不見的人」帶出主題；第二段有擔任提詞員、國王忘詞時低聲提示的完整故事，理由（個性合適、幕後能看見全局）與讓步（演員得掌聲）俱全，結尾回扣題目。句型多樣、無文法與標點錯誤，用字精準（prompter、froze、credit、behind the scenes）。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段依序寫台上演員、左側後台提詞者、台下評審與觀眾，與圖相符；第二段有擔任提詞員、國王忘詞被提醒的具體經驗，並以 First、Second 說明偏好幕後的理由，結尾回扣題目。文法正確、時態恰當，但句型偏簡單；第二個理由（以安靜的方式幫助全隊）較籠統，用字準確但範圍偏窄（backstage、behind the scenes 重複）。
